assumptions: Per-shop status gets a third value "snapshot" (besides "live" and "snapshot-fallback") for shops served in snapshot mode, so the web can show the fallback note only for a real fallback.
`count` in shops[] is the number of that shop's products actually served (max 10), not the number fetched upstream.
GET /api/products/:id looks up the served (visible) list, so it and the future basket agree on what exists; the 404 body is exactly { error: "Product not found" }.
Invalid DATA_SOURCE values make loadConfig throw Error('DATA_SOURCE must be "live" or "snapshot", got "<value>"') (fail fast) rather than silently defaulting to live.

Tilda reuses data-product-lid across records (1498486363994 is both "Філе індички, 1 кг" and "Домашня сметана, 0,5 л"); the adapter keeps the first occurrence so ids stay unique and the snapshot's sourceIds stay valid; a composite key is deferred to add-admin and recorded in design.md Risks.

Each Tilda store record also carries one `t776__product-full js-product` popup block per product with the same lid and fields; the spec states these are not cards, and the fixture keeps them for the 5 kept products as a stricter test.

The karashynyard `unit` is derived from the product name by a quantity regex ("1 кг", "800 г - 1,1 кг", "10 шт"), matching how the committed snapshot's units were produced; empty when the name has none.

The osio description rule (collapse whitespace; if > 300 chars cut at the last space before 300 and add "…") was reverse-engineered from all 10 snapshot entries so live and snapshot entries are identical for the same product.
Snapshot fallback is per shop; if both the live fetch fails and the committed snapshot file is missing, the API may 500 — treated as a deployment error, not specified.

No new dependencies: the Tilda page is parsed with regular expressions over its stable markup; React Router data mode (createBrowserRouter / RouterProvider / Outlet / createMemoryRouter, confirmed via Context7 /websites/reactrouter) is used for routing.
The real adapters in server.ts use a 10 s AbortSignal timeout on fetch; a timeout surfaces as a typed failure and triggers the snapshot fallback.
The two staged fixture files live in the session scratchpad (not in the repo) because this workflow is planning-only; task 1.1 includes a regeneration recipe in case the scratchpad is gone.

findings.issue: D2 prescribes the unit regex `/\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?(?:\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л))?(?:\s*-\s*\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)?\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л)\b/u`. In JavaScript `\b` is ASCII-only (Cyrillic letters are not `\w`), so after a Cyrillic unit word followed by end-of-string or a space there is no word boundary. Verified in Node: the regex matches NONE of the 10 snapshot names ("Філе індички, 1 кг" → no match, "Фермерське курча 800 г - 1,1 кг" → no match, etc.). The scenarios "Fixture page yields its products in page order" (unit: "1 кг", unit: "800 г - 1,1 кг") and the design's own claim ("gives '1 кг', '800 г - 1,1 кг', '1 -1,5 кг', '10 шт', '100 г'") would fail against a parser that copies this regex.
findings.fix: Replace the trailing `\b` with a Unicode lookahead: `/\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?(?:\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л))?(?:\s*-\s*\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)?\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л)(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/u`. Verified: this reproduces all 10 snapshot `unit` values exactly and yields "0,5 л" for "Домашня сметана, 0,5 л".

findings.issue: D4 says `findProduct` "searches the served list". The catalog-api scenario "Known id" sends `GET /api/products/osio:6abcf192b7db2532803d266d` on a fresh app in snapshot mode with no prior `GET /api/products` and expects 200. If "served list" means the result of the last `load()`, a cold service has nothing served and the route answers 404 — the test outcome depends on an unstated reading of the design.
findings.fix: D4: define `findProduct(id)` as `(await load()).products.find((p) => p.id === id)` (so it goes through the same mode/cache/fallback path and works cold). catalog-api spec, scenario "Known id": add to WHEN "with no prior request to `GET /api/products`".

findings.issue: Scenario "Second load within five minutes reuses the cache" (line 79) never states what the fake adapters return. The THEN ("called once after the second load and twice after the third") holds only if the karashynyard fake returns `ok: true`; the sibling scenario "A failed fetch is not cached" shows that an `ok: false` fake is called on every load (three times here). Two valid readings of the WHEN give opposite results.
findings.fix: WHEN: "the catalog runs in `live` mode with an injected clock, a cache created as `createTtlCache({ ttlMs: 300000, now })` on the same clock, both fake adapters returning `{ ok: true, products }` with their 10 snapshot products on every call; `load()` is called at `now = 0`, `now = 299000`, `now = 300000`". Keep the THEN; optionally add "and the osio fake likewise once then twice".

findings.issue: D4 declares `selectVisibleProducts(perShop: ShopProducts[]): Product[]` but `ShopProducts` is defined nowhere in design.md, the specs or the shared-schema list (D10). The scenario "Selection keeps the first ten of each shop in order" is a pure-function test written before the implementation (tasks 1.6), so the test author has to invent the input shape (`{ key, products }`? `{ shop: ShopInfo, products }`? a Map?).
findings.fix: In D4 (and tasks 4.3) define and export `type ShopProducts = { key: ShopKey; products: Product[] }` from `src/lib/catalog.ts`; in the scenario WHEN write the call literally: `selectVisibleProducts([{ key: "karashynyard", products: <the 12> }, { key: "osio", products: <the first 3 snapshot products> }])`.

findings.issue: Requirement "Catalog page lists products by shop" (line 10) contains no SHALL for the loading state, the error state or the per-shop fallback note, yet three of its four scenarios ("Loading state", "Error state", "Snapshot fallback note per shop") test exactly those behaviours — scenarios without a governing requirement sentence. It is also silent on `status: "snapshot"` (chosen snapshot mode): whether the note shows is decided only in design.md D9/D10, and no scenario asserts it.
findings.fix: Add `### Requirement: Catalog page states` with: "While `getProducts()` is pending the page SHALL render an element with `role=\"status\"` showing \"Завантажуємо каталог…\" and no product list; when it rejects the page SHALL render `role=\"status\"` \"Не вдалося завантажити каталог\" and no product list; a shop whose `status` is `\"snapshot-fallback\"` SHALL show \"Показано збережену копію\" with `role=\"status\"` inside its section; shops with `status` `\"live\"` or `\"snapshot\"` SHALL show no note." Move the three scenarios under it and add one: "Chosen snapshot mode shows no note — WHEN `getProducts()` resolves with the 'Two shops with products' response but `source: \"snapshot\"` and both shops `status: \"snapshot\"` THEN no element with `role=\"status\"` is rendered and all 3 cards are" (tasks 1.9 then lists 5 tests).

findings.issue: Scenario "Runtime switch to snapshot" (line 44) is written at HTTP level ("`GET /api/products` is requested … the body has `source`"), but tasks.md 1.6 files its test in `apps/api/src/lib/catalog.test.ts` next to the service-level `load()` scenarios, while every other HTTP-level scenario is in 1.7 `products.test.ts`.
findings.fix: Either reword the scenario to the service level ("`setSource(\"snapshot\")` is called and then `load()` — THEN the result has `source: \"snapshot\"`, both shops `status: \"snapshot\"`, `count: 10`, fakes not called") or move the test name to tasks 1.7 and change 1.6 to three tests.

findings.issue: Scenario "Unknown id" (line 110) does not state the data-source mode or what the fake adapters return; in live mode the answer would depend on fakes the scenario never describes.
findings.fix: WHEN: "the catalog runs in `snapshot` mode over `data/shops/` and `GET /api/products/osio:000000000000000000000000` is requested".

findings.issue: Scenarios "Both shops live" (line 56) and "Selection keeps the first ten…" (line 95) use sourceIds `1629901938947` and `1636965991022`, which are not in `data/shops/*.json` (openspec/config.yaml: use ids from data/shops, not invented). They are real — cards 3 and 4 of `rec638772397` in the 2026-10-04 capture, prices 665 and 595 — but the scenario gives only name and price, so the test must fill `imageUrl`, `productUrl`, `description`, `category`, `unit` itself.
findings.fix: Say so in the WHEN: "followed by two more products (real lids from `rec638772397`, deliberately outside the snapshot) built by copying `products[0]` of the snapshot and overriding `sourceId`/`id`/`name`/`price` to `1629901938947` / \"karashynyard:1629901938947\" / \"Філе зі стегна індички, 1 кг\" / 665 and `1636965991022` / … / \"Стегно індички, 1 кг\" / 595".

findings.issue: D5 `createSnapshotSource(dir)` → `read(key)` does not say whether `read` is synchronous or returns a `Promise<Product[]>`; the 1.4 test ("Snapshot product normalizes to a Product") must be written before the module exists.
findings.fix: State the signature in D5 and tasks 4.1: `read(key: ShopKey): Promise<Product[]>` (memoized per key).

findings.issue: Tasks 1.4, 1.6 and 1.7 say "snapshot dir `data/shops`". As a relative path this resolves only because `pnpm test` runs `vitest run` from the repo root (root vitest.config.ts `projects`); it breaks if a test is run with another cwd, and D7 already resolves the same directory from `import.meta.url` in config.ts.
findings.fix: In those tasks: "snapshot dir resolved in the test as `fileURLToPath(new URL(\"../../../../data/shops/\", import.meta.url))` (from `apps/api/src/lib/`; one `../` fewer from `src/routes/`)".

findings.issue: Scenario "Two shops with products" (line 25) asserts the text "1 кг" is shown, but two of the three cards have unit "1 кг" (Філе індички and Каре молочної телятини), so Testing Library's `getByText("1 кг")` throws on multiple matches.
findings.fix: Write "the text \"1 кг\" is shown twice (`getAllByText` length 2)", or keep single matches by stating the expected count for each text.

findings.issue: Task 1.8 stubs `fetch` with `vi.fn(...)` but neither the spec ("validates the JSON body") nor design 6.1 says whether the client reads `res.json()` or `res.text()`; a stub that implements only one of them passes or fails depending on the implementation choice.
findings.fix: Task 1.8: stub resolves `new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status: 200, headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } })` (and `new Response("", { status: 503 })` for the failure) and asserts `vi.mocked(fetch).mock.calls[0][0] === "/api/products"`.

findings.issue: Decision 2 prescribes the unit regex `/\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?(?:\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л))?(?:\s*-\s*\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)?\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л)\b/u`. In JavaScript `\b` is ASCII-only even with the `u` flag, so a boundary after a Cyrillic unit word never exists; the regex matches none of the 10 snapshot names (verified with node: all 10 return NO MATCH). An implementer following the design gets `unit: ""` for every karashynyard product, contradicting the scenario values `unit: "1 кг"` / `"800 г - 1,1 кг"` in specs/shop-adapters/spec.md and the snapshot test in specs/catalog-api/spec.md.
findings.fix: Replace the trailing `\b` with a Unicode-aware lookahead: `/\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?(?:\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л))?(?:\s*-\s*\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)?\s*(?:кг|г|шт|мл|л)(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/u` — verified to yield exactly the snapshot `unit` for all 10 names, including "1 -1,5 кг" and "100 г (99 чашок)" → "100 г".

findings.issue: Task 7.1 is a `- [ ]` checkbox that requires `pnpm dev` (a foreground watcher) and `curl`, neither of which is in the loop's allow-list (scripts/loop.mjs `allowed`: pnpm check/test/typecheck/lint/spec:check/hooks:selftest, openspec, check-verdict, git status/diff) nor in .claude/settings.json. `pnpm loop` exits only when every `- [ ]` is `[x]` and the gate is green, so the agent can never honestly close 7.1 (and 7.2, which depends on its proof); the loop burns its 5-iteration budget or the agent ticks the box without evidence. The automated proof of the same behaviour already exists in the 1.7 route scenarios.
findings.fix: Remove the checkbox from 7.1: turn it into a plain paragraph under section 7 titled "Human smoke run (outside the loop, after 7.3)" with the same curl one-liner and expected output, and reword 7.2 so the agent records the `pnpm test`/route-test evidence while the human appends the curl line after the smoke run. Keep 7.3 (`pnpm check`) as the last checkbox.

findings.issue: Task 1.1 sources both fixtures from a session-scoped scratchpad (`/private/tmp/claude-501/.../364dc8be-.../scratchpad/fixtures/`) that macOS purges, and its fallback is to re-capture the live sites. A re-capture cannot reproduce the values the specs hard-code from the 2026-10-04 capture: osio `products[1]` "Щавлик органічний, осінній " (id 69f4bded4a817ece3acb690b), `products[11]` id 6aa15f6d98ecadd65969cc45 price 315, the 12-item order, and the exact record set of karashynyard.html. If the folder is gone before `/opsx:apply`, 5 adapter scenarios become unsatisfiable as written and the loop prompt forbids editing the spec. (Today the folder exists and all spec values match it — verified.)
findings.fix: Before apply, copy `karashynyard.html`, `osio.json` and `make-fixtures.py` (as provenance) from the scratchpad into `apps/api/fixtures/` and commit them (they are test data, not implementation). Reduce 1.1 to the three verification commands, and delete the "If that folder is gone, rebuild…" fallback. Also note the verification uses `node -e`/`grep`, which are not allow-listed — use the Grep tool and `pnpm test` instead, or mark the greps as human-run.

findings.issue: The requirement text and the "Fixture page yields its products in page order" WHEN describe the popup as `<div class="t776__product-full js-product" data-product-lid="…">` "carrying the same li_title__/li_price__ fields". In the actual fixture the tag is `<div id="t776__product-<lid>" class="t776__product-full js-product" style="display:none;" data-product-lid="<lid>">` (id before class) and the popup repeats only `field="li_price__<lid>"`; its title has no `field` attribute (li_title__ count is 5 for 5 cards, li_price__ is 10). A test author who greps for the spec's literal gets 0 matches.
findings.fix: Reword to: "one `<div id="t776__product-<lid>" class="t776__product-full js-product" … data-product-lid="<lid>">` popup block per card, repeating the lid and the `li_price__<lid>` field (not `li_title__`), which is not a card".

findings.issue: Scenario "Runtime switch to snapshot" is phrased at the HTTP level ("then `GET /api/products` is requested … the body has `source: "snapshot"`"), but tasks.md 1.6 places its test in `apps/api/src/lib/catalog.test.ts` against `load()`. The project's spec-reviewer treats a test that asserts different inputs than the scenario as NOT covered.
findings.fix: Either reword the scenario to "and `load()` is called → the result has `source: "snapshot"` …" (matching the two cache scenarios), or move the test to 1.7 `products.test.ts` through `createApp({ catalog }).request("/api/products")`.

findings.issue: The business requirement says the category is "the text of the nearest preceding record's t-title / t-name"; the spec narrows it to `t-title` only without saying why. In the fixture `t-name` occurs only inside store cards (`t776__title t-name`, `t776__price … t-name`), so applying the requirement literally across all records would mis-assign categories — the narrowing is correct but silent.
findings.fix: State it explicitly: "`category` = text of the nearest preceding non-776 record's `t-title` (or `t-name`) element; `t-name` elements inside store (776) records are product fields, not headings".

findings.issue: Scenarios "Both shops live" and "Selection keeps the first ten" use sourceIds `1629901938947` (665) and `1636965991022` (595), which are not in data/shops/*.json; openspec/config.yaml rule: "Use the product ids and prices from data/shops/*.json in scenarios, not invented ones". They are real (present in the 2026-10-04 capture of rec638772397) but nothing in the artifacts says so.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the requirement: "The two extra karashynyard ids come from the 2026-10-04 capture of rec638772397 (products 11–12 of that record) and are deliberately absent from the snapshot so the ten-limit is observable"; or pad with osio fixture items 1–2 (69f4bded4a817ece3acb690b, 6a282bd96624ab942057d43c), which are committed in apps/api/fixtures/osio.json.

findings.issue: Tasks 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 and 1.7 say the tests pass "snapshot dir `data/shops`" / read the fixture file, i.e. relative paths that depend on `process.cwd()`. Vitest projects do not chdir, so this only works when `vitest` is launched from the repo root; AGENTS.md requires tests to not depend on the environment.
findings.fix: Specify in 1.2/1.4/1.6/1.7: resolve paths from the test file, e.g. `fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../../data/shops", import.meta.url))` and `new URL("../../fixtures/karashynyard.html", import.meta.url)`.

findings.issue: Decision 7 adds a `SNAPSHOT_DIR` environment override that no requirement asks for and that is "used by nothing yet"; the agent cannot document it because `.env.example` is hook-protected, so it would ship undocumented.
findings.fix: Drop `SNAPSHOT_DIR`; keep `snapshotDir` as a plain `AppConfig` value defaulting to `<repo>/data/shops` (tests already inject the directory as a value).

findings.issue: Decision 4 injects both `cache` and `now` into `createCatalogService({ source, shops, snapshots, cache, now })` while Decision 6 gives the cache its own `now`. The cache scenarios say "with an injected clock"; if a test passes `now` to the service but builds the cache with `Date.now`, the TTL scenario at now = 300000 fails for a reason unrelated to the code.
findings.fix: Have the service own the cache: `createCatalogService({ source, shops, snapshots, now, ttlMs = 300_000 })` creating `createTtlCache({ ttlMs, now })` internally; drop `cache` from the public signature and update tasks 1.6/4.3/5.2 accordingly.
